name: Ui_SlideWindow_Ctor
signature: Ui_SlideWindow* Ui_SlideWindow_Ctor(void* heapCtx, void* layoutRef, u32 mode, u32 variant)
summary: Allocating constructor of the UI slide window: creates the object through the shared sprite-object allocator, installs vtable 0x773348 (primary) plus the secondary vtable at +0x258, marks the slide state byte at +0x2c8 as unused (0xff), enables the +0x2c9 flag and stores a 4.0 scalar at +0x2cc.
evidence: Sole literal-pool user of vtable 0x773348; that table's slots 46..48 are Ui_SlideWindow_CommitIfSliding (0x471CE0), Ui_SlideWindow_UpdateSlideStateB (0x471648) and Ui_SlideWindow_OnEvent (0x471820), all of which read the same +0x2c8 slide-state byte this function writes. Allocates via 0x28EE8C(heapCtx, {tag}) and sets a 4.0f (0x40800000) constant. No direct callers: it is reached through a virtual factory.

name: Actor_Animation_PlayIdleNut
summary: Stops whatever animation the actor is playing and starts the 'Nut' idle animation. Used to return an NPC/actor to its neutral standing pose.
evidence: Calls actor vtable+0x88 (stop animation) then vtable+0x84 (play named animation) with the literal at 0x472334, which is the ASCII string "Nut" - the idle pose name also seen in the reference translation notes. Listed in the animation-callback table at 0x725E38.

name: Actor_Animation_PlayRunAndCheckArrival
summary: Stops the current animation, starts 'Run', and when the actor's stored distance (+0x2e4) has reached zero asks the owner (vtable+0x98) to advance to the next behaviour state.
evidence: Same stop/play pair as 0x472304 but the animation literal at 0x472390 is "Run"; the guard is `if (0.0f <= actor->f_b9) vtable[0x98](actor)`, i.e. arrival test. Neighbours are Gfx_SpriteActor_* helpers.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_UpdateScreenPosition
summary: Per-frame motion integrator for a sprite actor: advances a scalar speed (+0x2e8) by the frame delta, then rebuilds the 2D screen position (0x9c..0xa4) from the base position plus the rotated follow offset. When the speed budget is exhausted it asks the owning motion state to finish and releases the sub-actor. Always returns 1 (stay alive).
evidence: Uses self->f_13 (the motion/controller object) for the frame delta at +0x10, calls the vector rotate helper 0x665564, stores X/Y/Z into the actor screen-position block 0x9c/0xa0/0xa4 (the block Gfx_SpriteActor_* functions read) and sets the redraw flag f_46; the else branch calls vtable+0x40(self,4) and controller vtable+0x14(sub,0).

name: maybe_Ui_Window_FinishCloseTransition
summary: Tells the window's transition child (+0x4c) to jump straight to its finished state and reports 0 so the caller knows no further work is needed. Appears to be the 'snap to end' half of the open/close animation.
evidence: Single indirect call `vtable[0x18](self->f_4c, 1)`; vtable 0x7735EC slot 1, whose slot 0 is Ui_Window_CloseAndHide (0x28ED30) - i.e. this is the window class's transition virtual.

name: Gfx_SpriteNode_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the sprite-node class: runs the shared Actor2D node destructor (which restores the base vtables at +0 and +0x258) and then frees the block.
evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x773540; the called 0x28EFB4 rewrites the vtable pointers at +0x258 and the secondary +0xD4 and calls 0x4AF56C; 0x10F6CC is the engine's 'destroy object' helper (vtable[1] of the object header). Slot 1 of the same table is 0x4721C4, slot 10 is 0x472450, both Gfx_SpriteNode_*.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteNode_EmitBurst_Tail
summary: Continuation block of the sprite-burst spawner: stores the freshly created effect node at +0x2f4 and returns; the following block is the retry path that re-plays the spawn animation when the requested effect id is not loaded yet. Ghidra split this tail off the main body.
evidence: The ARM code at 0x47298C is `bl 0x35FF3C; str r0,[r4,#0x2f4]; add sp,#0x68; pop {r4,r5,r6,pc}` and is preceded by the body of Gfx_SpriteNode_EmitBurst (0x47285C); the trailing branch 0x47299C re-enters via vtable+0x84 with an animation name. Ghidra decoded it as Thumb and produced halt_baddata, so the readable C is unusable.

name: Gfx_SpriteNode_CtorWithMotion
signature: GfxSpriteNode* Gfx_SpriteNode_CtorWithMotion(void* heapCtx, void* desc, u32 mode, u32 variant)
summary: Constructor for a sprite node that owns a floating-motion child: installs vtable 0x773630, zeroes the position, sets the two motion speeds (400 and 800 units/s), a -35 gravity-like acceleration and alpha 0xff, then initialises the embedded child object through 0x30C480 (the helper returns the child at +0x2f8, i.e. the object base is recovered as child-0x2f8).

name: Actor_SceneObject_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor for the actor scene object class (the object that carries an actor plus its 2D sprite parts): destroys the scene-object part and frees the memory.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_Begin
summary: Start method of the Dragon Jump action: stops the actor animation, sets frame 4, clears the jump flags (+0x14c..+0x14e) and requests the state (0, 2 or 5) that matches the actor's jump variant byte (+0x3f0), committing the request if accepted.
evidence: Slot 1 of vtable 0x773AB4 whose slot 0 is the action's deleting dtor and whose slot 3 (0x476C88) is its per-frame update; body calls actor vtable+0x80/+0x58(self,4), switches on `actor->f_3f0` 1/2/3 and uses the state-machine pair vtable+0x14(request)/+0x10(commit) on self+0x2c that all DragonJump states use.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_OnEvent
summary: Animation-event hook of the Dragon Jump action: event 13 (0xD, the end of the 'JumpM_Up_Loop' animation) raises the loop-finished flag read by the up-loop update.
evidence: Slot 6 of vtable 0x773AB4; body is only `if (arg2 == 0xd) self->f_14c = 1;` and f_14c is the flag guarded by Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpLoopUpdate (0x475CE4).

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpLoopUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the 'Dragon_JumpM_Up_Loop' segment: plays the loop animation, moves the actor along the stored velocity for the frame delta, and when the animation time budget is used up requests jump state 4.
evidence: Plays the literal string at 0x475DB8 = "Dragon_JumpM_Up_Loop"; the sibling state Actor_Action_DragonJumpMDownLoopUpdate (0x475DD4) does exactly the same with "Dragon_JumpM_Down_Loop", and both use velocity block +0x130..+0x140 and request state 4/7.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpAirDriftUpdate
summary: Airborne hold state: keeps adding a constant drift vector to the actor position each frame; when the remaining height (+0x3d8 - +0xa0) drops below zero it requests jump state 7.
evidence: Adds the float triple at 0x7E7024 to actor->f_100/104/108 scaled by self->f_140 (delta time) and compares `0.0 <= actor->f_3d8 - actor->f_a0` - the same height test used by the other DragonJump segments; uses state-machine request 7.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpEnd_Start
summary: Prepares the 'Dragon_JumpM_Up_End' segment: plays the end animation, converts the remaining horizontal distance and height into per-frame speeds over (animationFrames-2) ticks and stores the half-frame vertical step.
evidence: Plays the literal "Dragon_JumpM_Up_End" (0x47629C); divides the 2D distance by the tick count into self->f_13c and sets self->f_144 = -(dt / (ticks/2)) - exactly the fields the follow-up updates integrate.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJumpSEnd_Update
summary: Update for the short jump's landing segment: switches from 'Dragon_JumpS_End' to 'Dragon_JumpS_Loop' when the animation runs past frame 14, clamps the vertical speed so the actor cannot overshoot the ground, and requests state 8 when the tick budget runs out.
evidence: Plays literal strings "Dragon_JumpS_End" (0x47644C) and "Dragon_JumpS_Loop" (0x476460), gates the loop on func_00669DD4 (animation finished) and uses the same f_13c/f_138/f_134 velocity + f_140 delta-time integration as the other jump states.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_LerpToStartPose
summary: Eases the actor position and height toward the stored jump start pose at 0.15 per frame and then requests state 3; used as the recovery/return segment after a jump.
evidence: Lerp factor 0.15 (0x3E19999A) toward actor +0x3c8/+0x3cc/+0x3d0, sets the redraw flag f_118 and (if the segment-finished flag f_14c is set) requests state 3.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpEnd_Update
summary: Continuation of the 'M Up End' segment: counts the ticks down, keeps the vertical speed inside the remaining height, moves the actor along the horizontal velocity plus the vertical component, and requests state 8 when the timer expires.
evidence: Same field set as Actor_Action_DragonJumpMUpEnd_Start (f_148 ticks, f_13c/f_144) and uses the constant vector at 0x7E7024; decrements f_148 and shoots for actor->f_3e0/f_3e4/f_3e8.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_DragonJump_QueueEndState
summary: Jump segment that queues the landing state: when its tick budget expires it appends state id 8 to the action's pending-state array (self+0x40, count self+0x48) unless it is already queued; meanwhile it moves the actor and recomputes the vertical speed so the landing height is exact.
evidence: Contains the only in-batch use of the pending-state array (`*(int*)(base+i*4+0x14) == 8` with base = self+0x2c and count at self+0x48); uses func_0066A260 (animation frame) > 14 to switch into the final descent.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_AdvanceOnAnimEnd
summary: Short airborne segment: integrates the stored velocity each frame and requests jump state 6 as soon as the animation reports finished.
evidence: `actor->f_100 += f_130*f_13c` triple plus 0x669DD4 (animation finished test) then state request 6; same velocity layout as the neighbouring DragonJump segments.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_LerpAndRestart
summary: Eases toward the jump start pose at 0.2 per frame and restarts the action (state 1) once the elapsed time (+0x34) passes ~1.0 s.
evidence: Lerp constant 0.2 (0x3E4CCCCD) toward actor +0x3c8/+0x3cc/+0x3d0 and the guard `0x3E7FFFFF < self->f_34` (just below 1.0) requesting state 1.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the Dragon Jump action: advances the shared timer and the active element, invokes the element's bound delegate (9 element slots of 0x18 bytes at self+0x60), and when the action-finished flag is raised resolves the owning actor from the global id map and marks it (+0x314 = 0, +0x318 = 1).
evidence: Slot 3 of vtable 0x773AB4; walks `self + 0x2c + i*0x18` elements reading the delegate pair at +0x8/+0xC (pointer-to-member call idiom `*(code**)(fn + *adj)`), then uses the id-map lookup with mask 0x1FFFFF and table 0x7B80C0 also seen in 0x485108/0x4AF35C.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_End
summary: Stop method of the Dragon Jump action: stops the actor animation and puts it back on animation frame 4 so the actor returns to a neutral pose.
evidence: Slot 2 of vtable 0x773AB4; body is actor vtable+0x88 (stop) then vtable+0x54(actor,4), the same frame reset Actor_Action_DragonJump_Begin (0x475B2C) performs.

name: Actor_Action_DragonJump_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the Dragon Jump action (the +4 entry of the same function at 0x477270): overwrites the vptr, destroys the embedded element list and frees the object.

name: Monster_Action_Dulneigh_DtorDelete
